name: CoinPay Portal Wallet
summary: Non-custodial multi-chain wallet with one-click x402 payments and bulk payouts.
description:
CoinPay Portal Wallet is the browser wallet for coinpayportal.com, the CoinPay multi-chain payments platform operated by Profullstack, Inc. It is non-custodial and cross-browser (MV3).

This add-on is published by the operator of coinpayportal.com and is not affiliated with any other service using the CoinPay name.

- Create or import a BIP-39 wallet. The seed is encrypted at rest (WebCrypto AES-256-GCM + PBKDF2) and never leaves your device; signing happens inside the extension's background worker, so private keys are never exposed to a web page.
- Derives addresses for BTC, BCH, ETH, POL and SOL (with USDC on ETH/POL/SOL), matching the CoinPay web wallet.
- Backup-confirmation gate before the wallet is usable, plus a configurable idle auto-lock.
- One-click x402 (HTTP 402) payment approval for sites that request payment.
- Bulk payouts: a site can request many payments at once via window.coinpay.payBatch and you approve the whole run once, with per-payment progress — built for payables queues like ugig.net's accepted-invoice list.
- Sites connect per-origin and only after you approve the prompt.

Source: https://github.com/profullstack/coinpayportal/tree/master/packages/extension

chrome.singlePurpose: A non-custodial cryptocurrency wallet: it holds keys the user generates or imports, shows their balances, and signs payments the user explicitly approves — including HTTP 402 (x402) payment requests made by sites the user has connected.

permissionJustifications.storage: Stores the AES-256-GCM-encrypted seed vault, the user's per-origin site connections, and their settings (display currency, auto-lock timeout). Nothing is transmitted.
permissionJustifications.alarms: Drives the idle auto-lock timer that wipes the decrypted seed from session memory after the interval the user chose.
permissionJustifications.host:coinpayportal.com: The CoinPay API the wallet reads balances and transaction history from, and posts signed transactions to for broadcast.
permissionJustifications.host:ugig.net: ugig.net requests bulk payouts and x402 payments through window.coinpay; the content script must be injectable there for the provider to exist.

chrome.remoteCode: No. The build ships every script it executes; nothing is fetched and evaluated at runtime.

dataUse.notes: Wallet addresses and signed transactions are sent to coinpayportal.com to read balances and broadcast payments. The recovery phrase and private keys never leave the device. No browsing activity, no analytics, no personally identifying information.

firefox.privacyPolicyText:
CoinPay Portal Wallet is non-custodial. Your recovery phrase and private keys are generated on your device, encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM (PBKDF2, 600k iterations), and never transmitted anywhere — not to Profullstack, not to coinpayportal.com, not to any site you connect to.

What does leave your device: the wallet queries coinpayportal.com for the balances and transaction history of the addresses it derives, and posts signed transactions there to be broadcast to the relevant chain. That means wallet addresses and payment amounts are visible to that service, as they are to anyone reading the public blockchain.

The extension collects no browsing activity, runs no analytics, and contains no tracking code. It injects its provider only into origins listed in the manifest, and only exposes a wallet to a site after you approve that site's connection prompt.

Full policy: https://coinpayportal.com/privacy
firefox.reviewerNotes:
Build reproduction is in BUILD.md inside the source archive.

To exercise the extension without funds: open the popup, choose "Create new wallet", write down the phrase, confirm the three words it asks for, and set a password. The wallet view then lists a derived address per chain with zero balances. The payment-approval window (approval/index.html) is opened by the background worker when a connected site calls window.coinpay.payX402 or window.coinpay.payBatch; it never signs anything without an explicit click.

The bundled background/index.js is the vite output of src/background/index.ts and is not minified, so it maps line-for-line onto the TypeScript in the source archive.
